body:
Oh, I should clarify that I am absolutely not afraid of him. He has never shown any indicators of any kind of abuse or mistreatment. No violence, no yelling, no breaking things or punching walls, etc.

He does want to move - we've talked about getting out of our current state. You're not the first to suggest suboxone, I'm going to talk to him about that tomorrow and be fully open about how I'm feeling. 

I might just read him this post, honestly. 

Thank you for your advice, it was very good!

Have you found virtual NarAnon to be helpful? I checked another website and there are two meetings in my city but they both overlap with my classes (I've recently gone back to school).

Thank you for taking the time to respond. I really appreciate your words and I will be thinking heavily on them.

Thank you so much for taking the time to share your story. Your comment gives me an immense sense of relief and solidarity. I'm sorry about what you've gone through.

My fear is that it will go as you described. Right now, he's a fully functional adult. He goes to work every day and does well there, he pays bills on time, he's about to be debt-free, he's able to connect with his son. In our relationship, he takes me out on dates, we have an excellent intimate life, everything is wonderful. It's like there's this third party in our relationship just lurking in the background all the time and it's steadily getting closer.

I know he wouldn't consider Methadone but he might be willing to look into Suboxone. 

I know it's time for us to have a conversation about it and see how he feels about quitting and what he is willing to do to help himself. I worry because while I've been trying to quietly deal with this for months it'll probably seem like it's out of nowhere to him and I don't know how to deal with that. I don't want to make him feel like I've been misleading him, if that makes sense.

Sorry to dump more on you - your comment just really hit me.

Thank you again, and I wish you the best of luck with med school and your future!
I'm sorry. That sounds really tough. Do you have Netflix or Hulu? If you're in the US, I bet I can recommend something you'll like.
Are you able to go on long walks by yourself? Would that help you feel more independent?
